note: Patrick signed the three clusters not marked hypothesis on 2026-10-16 (R-0857, builds on R-0856). The two marked hypothesis are scored neither way: a try that stores one, or leaves it out, neither gains nor loses. The lake weekend is not a cluster, too short, an acute problem: a try that stores it misses. The 2001-04 cluster opens at the grandmother's illness (event 176), dated approximate: the diagram it copies gives the year as one of two, which R-0855 calls approximate; the copy had marked it unknown in error.

said.question: Thinking over your life up to now, which two or three stretches were the fullest or hardest, and roughly which years?
said.words: There are two stretches I'd pick. The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework. After that came years of performing and odd jobs on boats up and down the coast. The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school. I think something in the family set each of those off. I'd also like to know when my sleeplessness started; I've always been keyed up, maybe anxious, maybe more than that. And I wonder what the moves between primary and secondary school did to me. Before that it's a blur.
